protocol.name: wayluck_wm_unstable_v1

description.summary: a window manager placing windows for wayluck

protocol.description:
The contract between wayluck and the window manager. The window manager owns placement: where each window goes, what's shown and what isn't. wayluck owns clients, buffers and pixels, and applies what it's told.
Windows are placed in scenes, not on outputs. A scene is a set of windows at positions relative to its own top left corner, stacked in the order they were placed: a workspace, to a window manager that has them. An output shows one scene (or none), drawn from the output's top left corner; a scene may be shown on several outputs at once, each drawing it the same way (mirroring). What isn't in a shown scene isn't drawn.
A scene is laid out once, for one size (scene_size): a window has one size, whatever shows it. Showing a scene on an output of another size is allowed, but then it's cut off, or doesn't fill it.
Unstable: changed in place, without version bumps, until it's frozen as wayluck_wm_v1. A window manager and a wayluck from different commits may not understand each other.

interface.name: wayluck_wm_manager_v1

description.summary: the window manager's connection to wayluck

interface.description: Bound by the one window manager. On binding, wayluck sends an output event for every output and a window event for every window, then ready. After that, it sends them as they appear.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop managing

request.description: Windows keep their places until another window manager binds.

request.name: transaction

description.summary: start a transaction

request.description: Changes made through it are applied together on commit, or not at all.

request.name: scene

description.summary: make a scene

request.description: Empty, and shown nowhere, until transactions place windows in it and show it on outputs.

request.name: workspace

description.summary: make a workspace, for programs that list them

request.description: A workspace as programs that list them (bars, pagers) see it: what it shows is the window manager's own business (scenes), this is only what's said of it. Listed from now on, after those made before it: unnamed, on no output and not active, until transactions say otherwise. Destroyed, it's no longer listed.

request.name: virtual_output

description.summary: make an output with no screen behind it

request.description:
Clients see it as any other output (wl_output): screen sharing and screenshots can capture it. Nothing else happens on it: the pointer doesn't reach it.
No one looks at it, so it's only drawn when a capture asks for a frame (and, for screen sharing, something in it changed): the capturing client sets the frame rate. Windows in a scene shown only here are paced like they would be on template (its refresh rate), or at refresh with no template.
Bars, wallpapers and overlays: clients can't put their own on it (wayluck closes layer surfaces made for it). With a template, it draws that output's own around its scene, the same surfaces, as they are there: a workspace shared from it looks as it would on it. With no template, it draws none.
It isn't announced with an output event: its name, geometry, usable area (all of it: bars are template's business) and done follow on this object, as for any output. It goes when this object is destroyed. Its geometry is somewhere no monitor is.

arg.name: template
arg.summary: the output it's modelled on: whose bars, wallpapers and overlays it draws, and whose refresh rate paces its windows

arg.name: refresh
arg.summary: in mHz: windows' pace with no template

description.summary: modifier keys, as X numbers them

request.name: bind_key

description.summary: take a key combination from clients

request.description: While the binding exists, pressing keysym with exactly these modifiers (Caps Lock and Num Lock aside) goes to the window manager as pressed, and not to the focused client. A keysym matches the key as typed and as it is without modifiers, so shift+1 is bound as 1.

request.name: bind_button

description.summary: take a pointer button combination from clients

request.description: Like bind_key, for a mouse button: pressing it with exactly these modifiers goes to the window manager as pressed, and its release as released (whatever the modifiers are by then), not to the client under the pointer.

request.name: grab_pointer

description.summary: keep the pointer from clients

request.description: For a drag the window manager does itself (moving a window, say): until ungrab_pointer, no client sees the pointer move or its buttons. pointer_position keeps coming.

description.summary: give the pointer back to clients

request.name: warp_pointer

description.summary: move the pointer

request.description: To x, y in global coordinates, as if the user had moved it there: clients under it hear, and pointer_position follows. Nested in another session, that session's cursor stays where it is.

request.name: set_keymap

description.summary: the keyboard's layout, by XKB names

request.description: As in setxkbmap: an empty string is XKB's default (layout "us"). Clients get the new keymap, and key bindings match keys as it has them. A keymap XKB can't make is ignored.

request.name: set_layout

description.summary: switch to one of the keymap's layouts

request.description: By its place in set_keymap's layout list, from 0.

request.name: offer_workspace

description.summary: a workspace the user may share

request.description: An answer to picker_opened: one workspace the picker should list, under the monitor it's on (output), by name, with the windows in scene (laid out in it: offered workspaces should be laid out, the hidden ones too, until picker_closed). Offering a scene again replaces what was said of it. Offers after offers_done count for the next picker.

request.name: offers_done

description.summary: every workspace has been offered

request.description: The picker may show its list. Without this, it shows it anyway after a moment, with the workspaces offered by then.

request.name: set_animation

description.summary: how windows move to where they're placed

request.description:
For every window without one of its own (wayluck_wm_window_v1's set_animation), until it's set again. A window placed where it's on screen already (in the same scene) is drawn moving there, from where it's drawn then, over duration milliseconds; one appearing (placed in a scene it isn't in) appears where it's placed, unless the transaction says where it starts (start_from). A duration of 0: no animation, as before this is set.
How far along it is (0: where it starts, 1: where it's placed) follows curve: an array of 32-bit floats in the machine's byte order, how far along at evenly spaced times from the start to the end, 2 to 1024 of them (invalid_curve otherwise), straight between them. They may go past 0 or 1 (overshooting). At the end it's where it's placed, whatever the last one says. Its client is asked for the new size at once; what it draws is stretched to the rectangle it's drawn in meanwhile.
Placed again where it's going, it keeps going; placed somewhere else on its way, it goes there from where it's drawn then.

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: how strongly what's behind windows is blurred

request.description: For every window blurred behind (the transaction's blur), until it's set again. What's below it is halved passes times, then doubled back as many, sampled offset pixels apart each time: more passes reach farther (about offset times 2^passes pixels), a bigger offset is smoother. 1 to 8 passes, offset above 0 (invalid_blur otherwise). Until it's set: 3 passes, offset 2.

request.name: set_name

description.summary: the window manager's name, for programs that ask

request.description: Programs that ask which window manager runs (X's, as EWMH has it) are told this name. Until it's set, and once the window manager is gone: wayluck.

entry.name: not_own_toplevel
entry.summary: own_window's surface isn't a toplevel of the window manager's

entry.name: invalid_curve
entry.summary: an animation's curve isn't 2 to 1024 floats, all numbers

entry.name: invalid_blur
entry.summary: set_blur's passes aren't 1 to 8, or its offset isn't above 0

request.name: own_window

description.summary: one of the window manager's own surfaces, as a window

request.description: A surface of the window manager's own, with the xdg_toplevel role (made before this; committed or not), to draw something of its own among the windows: a preview, say. It's given a window object, as the window event gives others' windows, and isn't announced with one. It's placed, hidden, given a border and stacked like any other (and a transaction that resizes it waits for it to redraw), but it's never given the keyboard (focus on it is focus on none), and clients that list windows (foreign toplevel lists, the picker) don't see it.

event.name: unavailable

description.summary: another window manager is bound

event.description: This manager does nothing; the client should destroy it.

description.summary: a new output

event.name: window

description.summary: a new window

event.description:
A toplevel that wants to be shown, announced at its client's first commit (an X window: once Xwayland has given it a surface): its title, app_id, parent, size_hints and a fullscreen_request, as far as its client set them up, follow at once. Until a transaction places it, it isn't shown.
Its id is wayluck's name for it, in its log too: it stays the same for the window's life and isn't reused.

description.summary: everything that existed at bind time has been sent
the pointer moved here, in global coordinates

event.name: picker_opened

description.summary: the user is about to choose what to share

event.description: Offer the workspaces the picker should list (offer_workspace), then say so (offers_done). Wayluck draws the picker itself, over a monitor: it's no window. Not sent again until picker_closed.

event.name: picker_closed

description.summary: the user chose, or cancelled

event.description: Offered workspaces no longer need to be kept laid out (except one shared: share_workspace).

event.name: share_workspace

description.summary: the user chose to share a workspace

event.description: Sent before picker_closed. wayluck made output, a virtual output modelled on the monitor the workspace was offered on, showing scene (the scene it was offered with), for the portal to capture. Keep the workspace laid out while it's shared, and keep output showing the scene it's in (if that changes: shown, or not). When capture stops (capture_stopped: also sent if none starts within a few seconds), destroy output: it goes.

event.name: layer

description.summary: a new layer surface

event.description: A bar, wallpaper, notification or launcher (wlr-layer-shell), announced once it's on an output. wayluck places it, as its client asks; the window manager only gives it a look (a transaction's layer requests). Its namespace, layer and output follow at once, then done.

description.summary: a monitor

request.name: destroy

description.summary: forget the output (after removed)

request.description: A virtual output goes with it.

description.summary: its connector name, e.g. DP-1
where it is, in global coordinates
the events before this one describe the output's current state
the output is gone; destroy it

event.name: usable

description.summary: the part windows may use

event.description: What bars and panels (layer-shell surfaces' exclusive zones) leave of the output, in global coordinates: where windows should go. Sent with geometry, and again when it changes, before done.

event.name: capture_started

description.summary: someone is capturing it

event.description: A client asked for frames of it (screen sharing, recording): what it shows should be kept up to date. Sent once, when the first capture starts.

event.name: capture_stopped

description.summary: no one is capturing it any more

event.description: Every capture of it stopped: no frame asked for in the last second, and none waiting for something to change. A virtual output nobody captures can go.

interface.name: wayluck_wm_scene_v1

description.summary: windows laid out together: a workspace

interface.description: Windows are placed in it by transactions (place); outputs show it (show). A window is in one scene at most: placing it in another moves it there.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: forget the scene

request.description: Its windows aren't in any scene any more (as after hide), and outputs showing it show nothing.

description.summary: a toplevel window
forget the window (after closed)
ask the client to close it

request.name: set_animation

description.summary: how this window moves to where it's placed

request.description: As the manager's set_animation, for this window only, whatever the manager's says, until it's set again or unset. A duration of 0: this window isn't animated. An invalid curve is the manager's invalid_curve error.

description.summary: move as the manager's set_animation says

event.name: closed

description.summary: the window is gone; destroy it

event.description: It's no longer shown, and placing it does nothing.

event.name: focus_request

description.summary: the user clicked it

event.description: wayluck doesn't focus it: the window manager decides, with a transaction's focus.

description.summary: the pointer is over it now
the pointer isn't over it any more

event.name: fullscreen_request

description.summary: its client asked to be fullscreen

event.description: F11 in a browser, say. Nothing changes unless the window manager makes it so, with a transaction's fullscreen.

description.summary: its client asked to stop being fullscreen

event.name: parent

description.summary: the window it belongs to

event.description: A dialog's main window, say (null: none). Sent with the window, and again when its client changes it.

event.name: size_hints

description.summary: the sizes its client can work with

event.description: Its client's smallest and largest size (0: no limit). The same smallest and largest: a window of one size, like a dialog or a splash screen. Sent with the window, and again when they change.

entry.name: utility
entry.summary: a palette or toolbox, for its application

entry.name: menu
entry.summary: a menu or tooltip it manages itself

entry.name: toolbar
entry.summary: a toolbar torn off its window

event.name: kind

description.summary: what kind of window it is

event.description: What its client says it is: an X window's type (_NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE; one without, with a parent: a dialog), a Wayland window's parent (with one: a dialog). The same for either, so a window manager treats them alike. Sent with the window, and again when it changes.

entry.name: above
entry.summary: to be kept above the others

entry.name: aspect
entry.summary: to keep its shape: width to height fixed

event.name: hints

description.summary: how its client would like it kept

event.description: What its client asks of its window manager, besides its size limits: an X window's _NET_WM_STATE (above, or on every workspace) and the aspect in its WM_NORMAL_HINTS (the smallest and largest the same). Sent with the window, and again when they change.

event.name: attention

description.summary: it wants the user to look at it, or no longer

event.description: Its client wants the user's attention: an X window urgent (WM_HINTS) or demanding attention (_NET_WM_STATE), or a Wayland window asking to be brought forward with no right to (xdg-activation, its token from no recent input of its own). Until it's focused, or its client says it no longer does. Sent with the window, and again when it changes.

arg.name: on
arg.summary: 1: it does, 0: it no longer does

event.name: workspace_request

description.summary: it's asked to be on a workspace

event.description: A program asked (a pager, or the window's own, by X's _NET_WM_DESKTOP) for it to be on workspace; null: on all of them. The window manager decides: window_workspace, or not.

event.name: activate_request

description.summary: it's asked to be brought forward

event.description: Its client asked, with the right to: a Wayland client with a token from input the user just gave it (xdg-activation), an X client or pager by _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW. The window manager decides: focus it, show its workspace, or not.

event.name: done

description.summary: that's all, for now

event.description: Sent once wayluck has said all it has to about the window for now: after what it comes with (names, parent, kind, size limits, hints, a fullscreen request), and after each lot of changes to them. A window manager decides with all of them, not some: placing a new window, say, after its first done.

description.summary: a key combination the window manager has
give it back to clients
the user pressed it
a pointer button combination the window manager has
give it back to clients
the user pressed it
the user let go of the button

interface.name: wayluck_wm_transaction_v1

description.summary: changes applied together

interface.description: Requests made before commit are collected, not applied. After commit, the transaction takes no more requests; wayluck answers with applied or failed, and then it should be destroyed.

description.summary: drop it; uncommitted changes are discarded

request.name: place

description.summary: put a window in a scene, at a rectangle

request.description:
Coordinates relative to the scene's top left corner. The client is asked to take that size; whatever size it commits, the window is drawn at x, y. If it was in another scene, it leaves that one.
Stacking: the windows a transaction places in a scene go above every other window in it, in the order they're placed, the last on top.

request.name: hide

description.summary: take a window out of its scene

request.description: It isn't drawn anywhere until it's placed again.

request.name: scene_size

description.summary: the size a scene is laid out for

request.description: Usually that of the output it's shown on. Previews scale a scene by it. A scene's size is 0x0 until it's given one: then it's drawn, but not scaled.

request.name: show

description.summary: what an output shows

request.description: A scene, drawn from the output's top left corner (null: nothing, only what's below windows, like wallpapers). Several outputs may show the same scene. An output shows nothing until it's given a scene.

description.summary: apply everything in this transaction, together

request.name: focus

description.summary: give a window the keyboard

request.description: With no window, no window has it. The focused window is drawn as active; where it stacks is up to place.

request.name: border

description.summary: draw a border around a window

request.description:
width pixels wide, outside the window's rectangle (place gives the rectangle inside it); 0 draws none. Colours are 0xAARRGGBB, one for each side. A window has no border until it's given one.
The rectangle's corners are rounded radius pixels (what the client draws there is cut off), and the border's follow them; 0: square.

request.name: shadow

description.summary: draw a shadow below a window

request.description: The shape of the window and its border (with their rounded corners), grown by spread pixels on each side (negative: shrunk), moved by x, y, and blurred about blur pixels each way, in colour 0xAARRGGBB. It's not drawn under the window itself, so a translucent window doesn't show it through. A colour with no alpha draws none; a window has none until it's given one.

request.name: outlines

description.summary: a scene's outlines, from now on

request.description: A scene's outlines (a group's, say) are those the outline requests after this one, in this transaction, add to it: none, if none do. A scene has none until it's given some.

request.name: outline

description.summary: draw an outline on a scene

request.description: A line line_width pixels wide along the inside of a rectangle (in the scene), in colour 0xAARRGGBB, below the scene's windows. Its corners are rounded as a border's: radius pixels on its inside, radius plus line_width outside; 0, square. Only what's inside the clip rectangle is drawn. Added to those an outlines request before it, in this transaction, started with.

request.name: tiled

description.summary: say which edges of a window are tiled

request.description: The edges that meet other windows or the output's: the client is told (xdg_toplevel's tiled states), and draws for it, e.g. without shadows, and without rounding its size to whole character cells. A window has none until it's given some.

request.name: fullscreen

description.summary: tell a window whether it's fullscreen

request.description: The client is told (xdg_toplevel's fullscreen state) and draws for it, without its own chrome. Where it goes, and how big, is still up to place. A window isn't fullscreen until it's told so.

request.name: instant

description.summary: a window this transaction places isn't animated

request.description: The window (null: every window this transaction places) is drawn where it's placed at once, and one on its way stops there: for a window dragged, say, placed again and again as the pointer moves, while windows making room for it are animated.

request.name: start_from

description.summary: where a window placed in this transaction starts

request.description: Drawn moving from this rectangle (x, y, width, height, relative to its scene's top left corner, as place's) to where it's placed, as its animation says (set_animation): a window appearing, sliding in or growing, say. It fails the transaction if the window isn't placed in it, or if a size isn't positive. Not animated (a duration of 0, or instant): it's ignored.

entry.name: client
entry.summary: where its client asks (ext_background_effect_v1), if it does

request.name: blur

description.summary: blur what's behind a window

request.description: What's below the window, blurred as set_blur says, drawn behind it (inside its rounded corners): seen where the window is translucent. Until it's told: client.

request.name: layer_corners

description.summary: round a layer surface's corners

request.description: Its corners cut off, rounded radius pixels, as a window's with a border's radius; its shadow and blur take that shape. Until it's told: 0, square. A layer surface gone by then is let be.

request.name: layer_shadow

description.summary: draw a shadow below a layer surface

request.description: As shadow, for a layer surface: around its shape (layer_corners).

request.name: layer_blur

description.summary: blur what's behind a layer surface

request.description: As blur, for a layer surface. Until it's told: client.

description.summary: name a workspace

request.name: workspace_output

description.summary: say which output a workspace is on

request.description: Null: none in particular.

description.summary: say what state a workspace is in

request.name: window_workspace

description.summary: say which workspace a window is on

request.description: Null: on all of them. Until it's told, and once its workspace is destroyed, nothing is said of it.

description.summary: the changes are on screen

event.name: failed

description.summary: nothing was applied

event.description: For example, a window in it was closed first.

description.summary: a layer surface: a bar, wallpaper, notification
forget it (after closed)

event.name: namespace

description.summary: what its client calls it

event.description: Its client's name for what it is ("waybar", "notifications"): the same for its life. Sent with it.

event.name: layer

description.summary: which layer it's on

event.description: Background and bottom: below windows; top and overlay: above them. Sent with it, and again when its client moves it.

event.name: output

description.summary: the output it's on

event.description: Sent with it (null: an output the window manager doesn't know).

event.name: done

description.summary: that's all, for now

event.description: After what it comes with, and after each lot of changes.

description.summary: it's gone; destroy it

interface.name: wayluck_wm_workspace_v1

description.summary: a workspace, as programs that list them see it

interface.description: Made by the manager's workspace request; what's said of it, by transactions.

description.summary: it's no longer listed

event.name: activate_request

description.summary: it's asked to be shown

event.description: A program asked: a bar or a pager, by X's _NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP. The window manager decides: show it, or not.
